title: Fix nested-function double-counting in complexity gates (outer wrapper inherits inner closure's score)
problem: checks/complexity.py collects nested defs via _functions() (ast.walk over the whole tree) and then cyclomatic()/cognitive() also walk the full node subtree — so a wrapper function's score includes the bodies of its nested closures, while the closure itself is scored again separately. Verified empirically: `def outer(): def inner(): if a: if b: if c: ...` yields outer cyclomatic=4/cognitive=6 even though outer's own body is a single return, and inner scores 4/6 too. This diverges from gocyclo/gocognit semantics (nested functions scored as separate units) and produces false-positive gate failures on wrappers/decorator factories, which pressures teams to widen the blunt substring ignore_patterns (checks/config.py:is_ignored) and mask real complexity.
acceptance: New regression test in checks/test_complexity.py: a wrapper function containing a nested complex closure scores cyclomatic==1 and cognitive==0 while the inner closure scores its own branches (no double count)
python -m pytest checks/test_complexity.py passes (49 checks/ tests stay green)
python cli.py check-complexity still exits 0 on the current repo tree (no new ignore_patterns entries needed)

title: Add machine-readable --json output to the four harness gates (cli.py check --json)
problem: The four gates (filesize/complexity/root-policy/style) only print human text and return an exit code (cli.py:37-67), while every other checker in the repo emits structured JSON (scripts/check-ui-spec.py --json, check-frontend-quality.py --json, check-knowledge-freshness.py --json, all registered as pi-batch.yaml validators) and pbatch/gate_fix.py consumes structured findings for the auto-fix loop. The harness gates therefore cannot feed automated fix loops, campaign scoring, rejected-artifact diagnostics, or LLM validators configured as 'python cli.py check' (pi-batch.yaml 'quick') — they get only free-form stdout.
acceptance: python cli.py check --json emits a single parseable JSON document (per-gate violation list with file:line and kind, plus counts) and preserves the exit code semantics
New regression test in checks/test_config.py (or a new checks/test_cli_json.py) asserts the JSON schema: one key per gate, values are arrays of strings
python cli.py check without --json produces byte-identical human output (backward compatible)

title: Validate engineering.yaml values with actionable errors naming the offending key
problem: Malformed config values crash get_config() with bare ValueError/TypeError (verified: max_lines: '500 lines' -> ValueError, max_cyclomatic: 'high' -> ValueError, max_files: null -> TypeError) because _load_* in checks/config.py call int() unguarded. Via cli.py the crash is swallowed into 'ERROR: {name} crashed: ...' without naming the key; invoked directly it is a raw traceback. Since engineering.yaml is documented as the ONLY file users edit when porting cli.py + checks/ to another project (engineering.yaml header, checks/README), the first failure mode new adopters hit is an undiagnosable one — the fail-closed exit code is preserved, but the diagnostic is poor.
acceptance: New test: engineering.yaml with filesize.max_lines: '500 lines' yields an error naming 'filesize.max_lines' (not a bare ValueError traceback)
New test: python cli.py check with a bad engineering.yaml prints 'ERROR: filesize gate config: filesize.max_lines must be an integer' and exits 1 (fail closed preserved)
Valid engineering.yaml parses to byte-identical Config values as today (no behavior change)
